primary_scope: English VPC.full, VPC.semi, and VID occurrence identification followed by uncertainty-bearing contextual fine-sense assignment

artifact.evidence: Exact train, dev, and test JSON paths, byte sizes, and SHA-256 values are pinned in benchmarks/streusle_v5_vpc_vid.json; no upstream data are bundled.

license.evidence: The release declares CC BY-SA 4.0 for MWE/supersense and redistributed UD annotations.

text.evidence: English Web Treebank review sentences and PTB annotations are redistributed upstream with Google and LDC permission; preserve that notice and do not place the corpus under this project's license.

span_category.evidence: Recoverable continuous/discontinuous members and strong PARSEME-derived V.VPC.full, V.VPC.semi, and V.VID categories support exact-span and category evaluation.

idiomaticity.evidence: Strong-MWE occurrence/category annotation is not a separate literal-versus-idiomatic decision.

fine_sense.evidence: Verb supersenses are broad semantic classes and are not OEWN/WordNet fine-grained contextual sense keys.

ambiguity.evidence: The release does not encode multiple plausible fine senses, abstention, or out-of-inventory decisions for a target occurrence.

split.evidence: UD train/dev/test splits are fixed. This project has already inspected the 40-item VPC/VID test projection and reported a baseline, so it is not an untouched blinded holdout.

artifact.evidence: The untagged snapshot contains a 56,622-row unfiltered JSONL file and filtered random/type-disjoint JSONL files; exact byte sizes and Git blob identities are recorded below.

license.evidence: The repository declares CC BY 4.0 at this snapshot.

text.evidence: Rows contain BNC- and PMB-derived context. Retain corpus provenance and attribution; no copy is needed in this repository.

span_category.evidence: Per-member character offsets and variant types are present for pre-extracted PIE targets, but there is no PARSEME VPC/VID category and the data do not test open-text candidate recall.

idiomaticity.evidence: The unfiltered release retains idiomatic, literal, other, unclear, and false-extraction evidence plus label distributions/confidence; filtered files retain at least 75%-confidence binary idiomatic/literal cases.

fine_sense.evidence: Its 'sense' labels distinguish usage classes rather than assigning occurrences to a reusable OEWN/WordNet fine-sense inventory.

ambiguity.evidence: Confidence, label distributions, unclear, and other preserve annotator difficulty, but do not encode multiple plausible dictionary senses or out-of-inventory judgments.

split.evidence: The filtered release provides both random train/dev/test and idiom-type-disjoint train/dev/test variants; the type-disjoint split is the only eligible generalization test here.

artifact.evidence: CSV data and evaluators are committed, but final test labels are not released. Subtask A dev text/gold Git blobs are 0e7d1ef24b88f898cf11450b6592b9d030bf861c and f7c42edbb040e724bc8bc9454a36451174648569.

license.evidence: The repository applies GPL-3.0; it cannot be silently relicensed into this project's permissive core.

text.evidence: Rows contain three-sentence web contexts; the paper separately names Wikipedia and CC-100 for Galician, but row-level source/right metadata are absent.

span_category.evidence: Each row supplies the target MWE string and context, not open-text member offsets, discontinuous spans, or VPC/VID categories.

idiomaticity.evidence: Subtask A collapses idiomatic plus meta usage against literal/non-idiomatic plus proper-noun usage.

fine_sense.evidence: Experts assigned occurrence-appropriate paraphrases during construction, but the released Subtask B is sentence/paraphrase similarity with no stable per-occurrence inventory sense ID.

ambiguity.evidence: Construction disagreements were discussed and unresolved cases discarded; the task does not expose ambiguous, abstained, or out-of-inventory outcomes.

split.evidence: Zero-shot MWE types are disjoint and one-shot supplies two examples per target type, but public gold is available for development rather than the final test.

artifact.evidence: Code is present, while processed data are Git LFS objects and get-data.sh fetches separate SemCor, PARSEME 1.1, DiMSUM, spaCy, and model artifacts without checksums or immutable versions.

manual_annotation_observation.deduplication: First accepted sentence-text plus word-index tuple, matching get_prodigy_annotations_to_apply

license.evidence: The official SemCor 3.0 archive grants use, copying, modification, and distribution with the retained Princeton notice. The MWEasWSD snapshot has a root AGPL-3.0 license and no separate data exception; CILI and OEWN mappings are CC BY. These layers must remain attributed and external to the permissive core.

text.evidence: The hash-pinned official SemCor 3.0 archive includes README and LICENSE files authorizing database reuse with the Princeton copyright, statements, and disclaimer on every copy. No SemCor sentence is bundled here.

span_category.evidence: The manual file has token indices and supports gaps, but has no VPC/VID category. Its 505 verb-POS rows are only a WordNet-underscore proxy, leaving zero directly category-confirmed VPC/VID rows.

idiomaticity.evidence: The learned alternative is a WordNet sense versus NOT_AN_MWE decision, not MAGPIE/SemEval literal-versus-idiomatic annotation.

fine_sense.evidence: Only 7 verb-proxy forms and 17 positive rows show more than one observed sense. Of 136 positive verb-proxy rows, 125 map losslessly to OEWN 2025 by exact sense ID plus CILI-confirmed ILI; two take_off rows retain the same ID while shifting ILI concept. No independent annotation/adjudication study is reported.

ambiguity.evidence: Rows force one sense or NOT_AN_MWE; multiple candidate options are shown, but multiple plausible senses, abstention, and out-of-inventory labels are not retained.

split.evidence: The manual annotation artifact has no split or document field. A retrospective split cannot supply missing categories, independent labels, ambiguity states, or an untouched holdout.

artifact.evidence: The exact 165,655,083-byte framework zip and its SemCor plus five source evaluation XML/gold pairs are SHA-256 pinned in the resolved audit.

license.evidence: The project publicly distributes the archive and requests framework/source-task citations, but the exact zip has no LICENSE file or explicit redistribution grant.

text.evidence: The evaluation texts inherit heterogeneous source-task provenance. No sentence or gold row is bundled; the separate official SemCor notice does not automatically license every evaluation set.

span_category.evidence: Multiword verb lemmas and head instances are present, but complete member spans are not reliably encoded. Target membership is restricted by one-category STREUSLE type overlap, not occurrence-level VPC/VID annotation.

idiomaticity.evidence: WordNet sense keys do not separately answer literal-versus-idiomatic status.

fine_sense.evidence: After unique STREUSLE type-category, exact-ID/same-ILI OEWN mapping, and at-least-two-candidate filtering, 23 occurrences across 18 VPC types remain; six are development and 17 are fixed source-test rows already exposed during audit.

ambiguity.evidence: One retained row has multiple acceptable gold senses, but the slice does not preserve usable abstention or out-of-inventory outcomes and only find_out contrasts senses across evaluation occurrences.

split.evidence: SemCor is training, SemEval-2007 contributes six development rows, and Senseval-2, Senseval-3, and SemEval-2015 contribute 17 fixed source-test rows; SemEval-2013 contributes none. The source-test labels were inspected during this audit and are not a blinded project holdout.

occurrence_evaluation.claim_ceiling: Exact English Web-review strong VPC/VID span and category performance, reported separately for continuous/discontinuous and train-seen/unseen types.
limits: Do not tune on the already inspected 40-item test projection or describe it as blinded.
Do not infer literal-negative, fine-sense, L2, register-general, or automatic-analyzer validity.
MAGPIE and SemEval test supplied idiom targets; they cannot substitute for open-text candidate-recall evaluation.

contextual_sense_evaluation.reason: The task-separated standard WSD slice supplies a tiny external conditional sense test, but no located resource provides an adequate joint or target-wide VPC/VID benchmark with occurrence spans, fine senses, ambiguity, abstention, and out-of-inventory outcomes.
contextual_sense_evaluation.resolved_reuse_lead: The MWEasWSD/SemCor audit found a lawful external analysis route but rejected the artifact as validation gold because it has zero category-confirmed VPC/VID rows, no independent annotation evidence or uncertainty states, order-dependent conflicting duplicates, sparse observed polysemy, and non-lossless OEWN mappings.
contextual_sense_evaluation.next_gate: Score transparent most-frequent-sense and gloss/rule baselines on the frozen 6-row development and 17-row source-test slice. Disclose prior label inspection and treat the result as a smoke-test floor, not blinded or full contextual-sense validation; keep BERT and new gold unauthorized until that check demonstrates a specific need.

secondary_contextual_idiomaticity.claim_ceiling: Type-disjoint supplied-target idiomatic/literal classification and error analysis; not candidate generation, PARSEME category, or fine-sense assignment.
